html:
A market town in the Gonja region of northern Ghana which became, in the 19th century, one of the largest markets in West Africa for kola nuts and enslaved people.

Asante traders brought kola north, and Hausa and other traders brought cloth, cattle and captives from the savanna. After Britain banned the Atlantic trade, many captives were sold into the north and into Asante itself. Wells where captives were washed before sale and a slave cemetery remain, and the town is part of Ghana's slave route heritage. Its trade declined after the 1874 war with Britain and civil war in Gonja. See also Dagbon and the Hausa.
sum: A market town in the Gonja region of northern Ghana which became, in the 19th century, one of the largest markets in West Africa for kola nuts and enslaved people.
